Complete these materials before our first live class on Thursday, September 10.
They establish the shared computational and statistical vocabulary we will use
throughout MECE 4520, using the course's recurring gas-turbine emissions
dataset. Plan for approximately 2.5–3 hours in total.

You can work in a local Jupyter environment or use the **Open in Colab** links.
Each notebook installs its only additional package and downloads the public
dataset itself, so it can be run independently in a fresh Colab session.

## 1. Course tools and Python foundations

**Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes

Learn the minimal NumPy and Pandas workflow used in the course: loading data,
selecting variables, filtering observations, and making a first plot.

[View the notebook](01-course-tools.ipynb) ·
[Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/changyaochen/MECE4520/blob/master/site/foundations/01-course-tools.ipynb)

## Before September 10

- Run every code cell in each notebook.
- Answer the questions marked **Check-in** in your own notes.
- Bring one observation or question about the gas-turbine data to the first live class.

## Dataset source

These notebooks use the [Gas Turbine CO and NOx Emissions dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/551/gas+turbine+co+and+nox+emission+data+set)
from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. The data contain 36,733 hourly
measurements from a gas turbine collected between 2011 and 2015 and are made
available under the CC BY 4.0 license.
